causes.fix: Increase wire feed pressure properly. Follow step 27 on page 17.
causes.test: Feed wire against wood 2-3 inches away; the wire should bend, not stop.

causes.fix: Flip roll to correct size. Follow the Feed Roller instructions on page 12.
causes.test: Check the Feed Roller groove matches the wire size marked on the spool.

causes.cause: Damaged MIG Gun, cable, or liner assembly.
causes.fix: Have a qualified technician inspect these parts and replace as necessary.
causes.test: Inspect the MIG Gun, cable, and liner for damage.

causes.fix: Loosen Feed Tensioner so it applies only enough pressure to prevent continued spinning after the Gun Trigger is released.
causes.test: Release the Gun Trigger and observe whether the wire continues to spin afterwards.

cases.symptom: Wire Feed Motor Runs but Wire Does Not Feed Properly

causes.cause: Gun cable is severely bent and Wire Feed mechanism cannot feed wire.
causes.fix: Straighten Gun cable.
causes.test: Straighten the cable and check whether the wire feeds.

causes.cause: Gun liner is clogged or worn.
causes.fix: Check gun liner for obstruction. Replace if necessary.
causes.test: Check the liner for obstruction or wear.

causes.cause: Gun liner is too small for welding wire being used.
causes.fix: Check that gun liner is correct size for wire.
causes.test: Compare the liner size with the wire diameter.

causes.cause: Wire is tangled on the spool.
causes.fix: Check wire for cross winding or tangled spool.
causes.test: Inspect the spool for tangled or cross-wound wire.

causes.cause: Wire is not making contact with Feed Rollers.
causes.fix: Check Feed Rollers and ensure correct groove for wire diameter is being used.
causes.test: Check the Feed Roller groove matches the wire diameter.

causes.cause: Feed Roller is not making enough contact with wire or is crushing flux-cored wire.
causes.fix: Check Feed Tensioner and ensure it is set properly.
causes.test: Check the Feed Tensioner setting; adjust per step 27 on page 17.

causes.fix: Adjust wire feed pressure properly. Follow step 27 on page 17.
causes.test: Feed wire against wood 2-3 inches away; the wire should bend, not stop.

causes.fix: Replace with the proper tip for wire used.
causes.test: Check the Contact Tip size against the wire diameter.

causes.cause: MIG Gun Cable Connector not fully inserted into Wire Feed mechanism.
causes.fix: Insert Gun Cable Connector properly. Follow steps 13 and 14 on page 13.
causes.test: Check the connector is fully inserted into the Wire Feed mechanism.

causes.fix: Have a qualified technician inspect and repair/replace as necessary.
causes.test: Inspect the liner for damage.

cases.symptom: Wire Creates a Bird's Nest During Operation

causes.fix: See first Troubleshooting section above (case 1).
causes.test: Run the case 1 checks: pressure, roller size, tensioner.

causes.cause: Incorrect Contact Tip or liner size or excessive wear.
causes.fix: Replace with the proper tip or liner size for wire used.
causes.test: Check tip and liner size and wear against the wire used.

causes.fix: Adjust wire feed speed to achieve a more stable arc.
causes.test: Adjust the wire feed speed and observe arc stability.

causes.cause: Loose MIG Gun cable or ground cable.
causes.fix: Check to ensure that all connections are tight.
causes.test: Check the gun and ground cable connections are tight.

causes.cause: Damaged MIG Gun or loose connection within Gun.
causes.fix: Have a qualified technician inspect and repair/replace as necessary.
causes.test: Inspect the gun and its internal connections for damage or looseness.

causes.cause: Incorrect polarity for process being run.
causes.fix: Ensure polarity is correct for operation: DCEP for MIG welding and DCEN for Flux-Cored self-shielded welding.
causes.test: Check polarity: DCEP for MIG, DCEN for flux-cored.

causes.cause: Gas coverage may be insufficient or too high.
causes.fix: Ensure gas flow rate is set according to Settings Chart. Make sure MIG Gun Cable Connector is fully inserted into Wire Feed mechanism with no O-Rings exposed.
causes.test: Check the gas flow per the Settings Chart and that the connector is fully inserted.

causes.fix: Check the ground clamp connection to the workpiece and machine. Ensure the MIG Gun is properly secured.
causes.test: Check the ground clamp contact with the workpiece.

causes.fix: Allow the unit to cool with the Power Switch ON; observe the duty cycle (page 19).
causes.test: Check the LCD for a thermal warning; let the unit cool with the Power Switch ON.

causes.cause: Circuit supplies insufficient voltage or amperage.
causes.fix: Check the input voltage and amperage against the Specifications table on page 7.
causes.test: Measure the input voltage and amperage; compare with page 7.

causes.fix: Check that the gun connection is seated; a qualified technician checks, secures, or replaces the Trigger.
causes.test: Check the Trigger connection is seated.

causes.cause: Low or over-voltage protection is active.
causes.fix: Check the input voltage is in range, then press the Reset Button on the back of the unit.
causes.test: Check the input voltage is in range, then press the Reset Button.

causes.fix: Select the correct mode for the process being run.
causes.test: Check the selected mode matches the process.

cases.symptom: Welder Does Not Function When Switched On

causes.cause: Unit not connected to outlet properly.
causes.fix: Connect the unit to the outlet properly.
causes.test: Check the plug is fully seated in the outlet.

causes.cause: Outlet is unpowered; breaker or GFCI tripped.
causes.fix: Determine and remedy the cause before resetting the breaker or GFCI.
causes.test: Check the outlet for power; check the breaker and GFCI.

causes.fix: Check the plug rating against the Specifications table on page 7.
causes.test: Compare the plug rating with the page 7 specifications.

causes.cause: Circuit breaker tripped from high input amperage.
causes.fix: Press the Reset Button.
causes.test: Check the breaker; press the Reset Button after remedying the cause.

causes.cause: Input Power Cord is not seated.
causes.fix: Ensure the twist-lock is fully secured.
causes.test: Check the Input Power Cord twist-lock is fully secured.

cases.symptom: LCD Display Does Not Light When Welder is Switched On

causes.fix: Check the ground clamp contact; clean the workpiece near the clamp and the weld location.
causes.test: Check the ground clamp contact and clean the workpiece.

causes.fix: Replace with a correctly sized Contact Tip.
causes.test: Check the Contact Tip size against the wire used.

causes.fix: Replace the Contact Tip if the hole is deformed or enlarged.
causes.test: Inspect the tip hole for deformation or enlargement.

causes.fix: Clean the Contact Tip.
causes.test: Inspect the tip for dirt or spatter.

cases.symptom: Wire Feeds, but Arc Does Not Ignite

causes.fix: Replace or refill the shielding-gas bottle.
causes.test: Check the gas bottle level.

causes.fix: Adjust the regulator to the correct gas flow.
causes.test: Check the gas flow at the regulator.

causes.fix: Clean the workpiece to bare metal.
causes.test: Inspect the workpiece for dirt, rust, or paint.

causes.fix: Reduce the contact-tip-to-work distance.
causes.test: Check the gun-to-workpiece distance.

causes.fix: Set the polarity: DCEP for MIG, DCEN for flux-cored.
causes.test: Check polarity: DCEP for MIG, DCEN for flux-cored.

causes.fix: Clean or replace the wire; check for rust or residues.
causes.test: Inspect the wire for rust or residues.

causes.fix: Check the line voltage and, if insufficient, have a licensed electrician remedy the situation.
causes.test: Measure the line voltage.

causes.cause: Improper gauge or length of cord.
causes.fix: Do not use an extension cord on this Welder. Use only one of the supplied power cords or an identical replacement cord.
causes.test: Check the cord is the supplied cord, with no extension cord.

causes.fix: Switch the current to the proper setting for metal thickness.
causes.test: Check the current setting against the metal thickness.
